LESSON: READING ALOUD

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: READING THEME 1: GREETINGS AND INTRODUCTION Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning 
Topic 2.1: Reading Aloud
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading Aloud, part of READING THEME 1: GREETINGS AND INTRODUCTION Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning  in Grade 5 MANDARIN.

Key inquiry question: Why are pauses important when reading aloud?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read out pinyin words on greetings and self- introduction using the correct tone 我、 你、 您、他、朋友、叫、什么、名字、是、不 是、女孩、男孩,

2. match personal pronouns with the correct corresponding images and read them out (他、我、你、它、我们、你们、 他们),

3. team up with peers to rearrange jumbled up sentences on greetings and introduction and read them aloud,

4. read out texts about simple introductions of self and others (name, age, gender) paying attention to punctuation marks and respond to the questions (你朋友叫什么名字? , 她是谁? 他是不是男、女孩?) collaboratively,

5. research online and offline the differences and similarities of punctuation marks in English and Chinese and share their findings.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read out pinyin words on greetings and self- introduction using the correct tone 我、 你、 您、他、朋友、叫、什么、名字、是、不 是、女孩、男孩,
2. match personal pronouns with the correct corresponding images and read them out (他、我、你、它、我们、你们、 他们),
3. team up with peers to rearrange jumbled up sentences on greetings and introduction and read them aloud,
4. read out texts about simple introductions of self and others (name, age, gender) paying attention to punctuation marks and respond to the questions (你朋友叫什么名字? , 她是谁? 他是不是男、女孩?) collaboratively,
5. research online and offline the differences and similarities of punctuation marks in English and Chinese and share their findings.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading Aloud together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: The learner interacts with digital technology to search for the differences and similarities of punctuation marks

in English and Chinese.

Values:
Unity: The learner collaborates with their peers to read and respond to questions on simple introductions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Analytical thinking skills: The learner develops analytical thinking skills as they rearrange jumbled up sentences on

greetings and introduction and reads them out.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner can relate their learning to Kiswahili and English on the use of punctuation guides when reading texts.
